title: Lockstep test pins a third copy of the terminal list, not the server's terminal_statuses const it claims to pin
evidence:
server/src/application/application_detail_handler.gleam:1286

const terminal_statuses: List(String) = [
  "form_completed",
  "manual_recorded",
  "unreachable",
  "refused",
  "objected",
  "partial",
  "failed",
  // v2-reserved voice terminal — harmless to include.
  "completed",
]

server/test/application/application_detail_handler_test.gleam:593-611

pub fn terminal_statuses_lockstep_with_shared_truth_test() {
  let terminal = [
    "form_completed",
    "manual_recorded",
    "unreachable",
    "refused",
    "objected",
    "partial",
    "failed",
    "completed",
  ]
  let non_terminal = [
    "queued",
    "skipped",
    "contact_initiated",
    "awaiting_correction",
    "scheduled",
    "calling",
  ]
  list.each(terminal, fn(s) {
    shared_reference_call.is_terminal_status(
      shared_reference_call.status_from_string(s),
    )
    |> should.be_true
  })

_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture-reference-checking-v1-2026-07-29.md

"A lockstep unit test pins the timeline's DB-string `terminal_statuses` list to the shared fn."
detail: Spec and arch doc claim the lockstep pin ties the server's `terminal_statuses` const to the shared fn; the test never references that const (it is private) and hardcodes a third copy. Drift between `terminal_statuses` (used at application_detail_handler.gleam:1454 for the legacy terminal fallback) and `is_terminal_status` would pass CI — the same third-copy lockstep pattern the AR-RC13 amendment itself describes.
recommended_fix: Export `terminal_statuses` (pub const) and have the test iterate the exported const instead of a local copy, so server-list drift from `is_terminal_status` fails the pin.
